experiment: E1 Tolman surface-brightness exponent n in SB ~ (1+z)^-n

standard_theory.source: Tolman 1930; FRW: rate (1+z)^-1, energy (1+z)^-1, angular size via D_A = D/(1+z) gives (1+z)^-2 more

model_prediction_derived_from_documents.derivation: HYPOTHESES 7/9 and paper sec.4: rate falls by 1+z (measured), phase rate falls by 1+z under the default per-link phase rule (measured, by construction), static lattice so angular size is s/D with no (1+z) factor, dilution 1/D^2 from open-3D ray runs. n = a + b where a = rate exponent, b = energy(phase-rate) exponent, geometric terms cancel.
model_prediction_derived_from_documents.lattice_measurement_plan: a and b fitted from loaded closed rows at D = 17.5, 41.5, 89.5 (z from 0.2 to 2.8), 12 rays each; dilution exponent and angular-size exponent vs D fitted in an open 3D box with and without a static uniform load (control that ray delay does not change geometry); zero-emission control must give a = b = 0.

observation.source: Lubin & Sandage 2001, AJ 122, 1084, raw exponents before luminosity-evolution correction, reduced under q0 = 1/2 expanding geometry
observation.note: later work (e.g. Sandage 2010 review) keeps 2.5-3.5 range; all reductions assume expanding geometry; values not re-reduced under a static-lattice metric (unverified for the lattice)

pass_fail.code_pass: all rays absorbed, quanta conserved, eye clock = ticks, zero-load control gives a = b = 0 and count dilution exponent -2 +/- 0.3 with and without load
pass_fail.model_candidate_falsified_if: the lattice-derived n differs from 2 by more than its fit error under reading B (then the paper's stated prediction is not what the engine does), OR the load changes the geometric exponents (dilution or angle) by more than their fit errors
pass_fail.verdict_rule: compare lattice n to 4 and to the 2.59-3.37 band; if lattice n < 2.59 - 2 sigma the data favour theory over the candidate; note that the data reduction assumes expansion
